sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 18.117 Topics in Several Complex Variables, Spring 2005, lecture notes prepared by Jonathan Campbell
sources.locator: Lectures 4, 7–9 and 11, PDF pp. 9–12, 18–23 and 23–25: local Dolbeault exactness, the projective atlas, sheaf/Čech cohomology, and Čech–Dolbeault comparison. The comparison proof is presented as a sketch and invokes the pseudoconvex Dolbeault theorem without proving it; it is contextual only. The chart map divides by the chosen homogeneous coordinate, so the standard chart condition is nonzero in that coordinate despite an apparent transcription error in the displayed condition.

sources.title: R. Dervan, lectures; Qiangru Kuang, notes, University of Cambridge Mathematics Tripos Part III, Complex Manifolds, Lent 2019
sources.locator: §3.1–3.2 and §4.4–4.5, printed pp. 9–11 and 23–26; §5, printed pp. 27–29. The Dolbeault theorem proof uses the local ∂-Poincaré lemma and smooth-sheaf acyclicity; Theorem 4.4 proves Čech comparison under acyclic-intersection hypotheses; the line-bundle and transition-function definitions are in §5. Its remark treats polydisc intersections, so it does not prove acyclicity of the projective intersections C^a×(C*)^b.
